_comment: Hand-maintained OpenAPI operations that the XSOAR 8 public API (/xsoar/public/v1) serves but the upstream demisto-py Swagger spec does not carry. Merged into xsoar.generated.json at build time by xsoar_mcp/openapi/__init__.py:load_merged() (collision-checked). Verified against a live XSOAR 8 hosted tenant (advanced Cortex API key) on 2026-11-24: all three return HTTP 200. The public API returns the parsed playbook definition (inputs/outputs/task graph), NOT the raw YAML source - there is no public YAML-export route callable with an API key. Note that of the /inv-playbook/* family only GET /inv-playbook/{investigationId} is served publicly; the other read variants (e.g. /inv-playbook/{id}/task, /inv-playbook/{id}/context) answer 404/303.

post.description: Search the playbooks installed in the tenant by name substring / free-text query. Returns matching playbooks (id, name, version, packName, ...); pass the returned id to getPlaybookById to read the full definition. Always pass a query: an empty query returns every playbook and each match carries its FULL task graph server-side (hundreds of KB before trimming). The API honours size and page, so cap a broad search with size (and page) rather than pulling everything. Records are trimmed to a compact set of fields by default.

query.description: Name substring / free-text filter to match playbooks against. Prefer a query; omitting it (or "") returns all playbooks.

size.description: Maximum number of playbooks to return. The API honours it; use it to cap a broad or empty query.

page.description: Zero-based page index, used together with size for paging.

get.description: Fetch one playbook's full definition by its playbook ID - the id returned by searchPlaybooks. For some playbooks the id equals the display name; for others it is a UUID, so resolve the id with searchPlaybooks first. Returns the parsed definition: inputs, outputs and the full task graph, which can be tens to hundreds of KB - fetch one playbook at a time. The public API does not expose the raw playbook YAML source; this is the structured definition.

Read the live execution state of the playbook run for one investigation (incident) - use it to monitor a running or finished playbook: which tasks ran, which are done/skipped/errored, and the timings. investigationId is the incident's id (the `id` or `investigationId` from searchIncidents). Returns the run's top-level state (id, playbookId, state, startTaskId, startDate, modified, netDurationMs, ...) plus a `tasks` object keyed by task id, where each entry carries its state (Completed / WillNotBeExecuted / InProgress / Waiting / Error / ...), timings, completedBy, retryCount, nextTasks (a map of branch label -> next task ids, e.g. {"#none#": ["104"]}) and the full task definition. Runs started from the tenant UI in test mode are visible here too. An unknown investigationId, or an investigation that has no playbook run, returns an empty object ({}) rather than an error - that is how 'no run' looks. Records are trimmed to a compact set of fields by default; pass fields ["*"] or ["tasks"]/["tasks.*"] for the untrimmed run/tasks map, and use `tasks.`-prefixed names (e.g. "tasks.task.name") to choose per-task fields.

parameters.name: investigationId
parameters.description: Investigation (incident) id whose playbook execution is read.

200.description: The playbook execution object: run metadata plus tasks{} keyed by task id.
